title: Schema-sanitizer stream guard and retry orchestration for function-call payloads
creator: Priya Ramanathan
description:
Problem:
When the runtime streams structured JSON for function/tool calls, partial truncation, tokenization escapes, or model-driven schema deviations cause downstream tool parsers to fail. This leads to failed tool executions, retries that cause duplicate side-effects, or silent data loss in orchestration flows.

Goal:
Build a runtime guard that performs streaming, schema-aware sanitization and an orchestration layer for idempotent retries of function-call payloads. The solution must be backward-compatible with existing SDKs (v1/v2) and provide clear developer-facing contracts for partial outputs, retry semantics, and compatibility shims.

Scope & non-goals:
- In-scope: streaming sanitization heuristics, lightweight in-band checksums, envelope versioning for function-call outputs, idempotency tokens for tool invocations, circuit-breaker for long-running/partial streams, SDK compatibility shim and server-side repair heuristics.
- Out-of-scope: replacing model-level generation behavior, wholesale protocol redesign for streaming envelopes (we will version instead), and complex ML-based repair models (may be a follow-up).

Design summary:
1) Streaming sanitizer: a low-latency pass that watches tokens and enforces an expected JSON schema envelope for function calls (name + args). It will automatically escape unbalanced quotes/braces and emit a "repair-sentinel" comment in the stream when on-the-fly fixes are applied.
2) Checkpoint + checksum footer: for streams longer than 1KB, the runtime will add periodic checkpoints (offset + CRC32) so the consumer can verify partial fragments and request a replay starting from last valid checkpoint.
3) Idempotent-retry orchestration: tool calls are annotated with an idempotency token generated by the runtime. If a retry is necessary due to truncation or transient network failure, downstream tool backends will be presented with the same token to deduplicate side-effects.
4) Circuit-breaker & graceful reflow: if repeated repairs exceed a threshold, the runtime will close the stream with a structured fallback object {"__fallback__": "incomplete", "reason": <code>} and route to a lower-fidelity model or an offline repair job.
5) Compatibility shim: SDKs that do not support the new envelope version will still receive a legacy-compatible text fallback; the server will include a header X-RI-Stream-Version.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end integration test that simulates 0.1% token corruption and shows >= 99.9% successful parsing after sanitizer repair or documented fallback.
- No increase in p50 latency > 10% for streaming endpoints in canary cluster.
- SDK compatibility matrix validated for SDK v1.3.x and v2.0-beta with explicit fallbacks.
- GitHub PR with implementation + unit/integration tests merged and runtime-1.22 release note drafted.

Metrics to track:
- sanitization_rate (repairs/sec), repair_success_rate, idempotent_retry_dedup_rate, fallback_rate, p50/p95 latency delta, customer-impact incidents linked.

Open questions:
- CRC32 vs SHA1 for checkpoints: CRC32 chosen for performance but we may upgrade per-tenant.
- Should repair-sentinel be visible to customers? We will default to internal-only flags but provide an opt-in verbose stream mode.
